svg.title: OPH particle atlas: from a loop to a detector
svg.desc: A horizontal illustrated dependency map with a protected-memory example, conditional spatial defect and field connections, preparation and quantum measurement diagrams, all Standard Model families, finite theorem premises and calibration-removal strategies. Dashed arrows mark unproved physical connections.
svg.text: FROM A LOOP TO A DETECTOR
OPH PARTICLE ATLAS / THE HORIZONTAL EXPLAINER
Follow the arrows. Read the assumptions beside them.
SOLID: a proved step under stated premises
DASHED: a physical connection to derive
BLUE: a supplied field model or calibration

The orange motif follows a candidate identity. Native loop memory, spatial winding and a measured particle are different mathematical objects. The dashed joins show exactly what must connect them; no complete defect-to-Standard-Model identification is asserted.
A round trip leaves a sign
same occupied ports; the two names swap
one history: 1/8; all other outcomes retained

Two named tokens move around three ports. Their unordered positions return to the start, but their ordering is exchanged. The
memory receives X. Its two coherent characters acquire signs +1 and −1. This is a concrete loop action that port counts alone

svg.text: EXACT PROTECTION UNDER THE STATED MEMORY LAW
Every retained repair outcome preserves the memory charge χ. Even an adaptive schedule cannot switch its two sharp sectors.
Protection means persistence under these allowed operations. A memory reset or an incompatible dephasing operation can remove it.
A particle candidate needs a local realization of the persistent difference and a law for creating and moving it. The illustrated
next step supplies a compact texture. Relating that geometric core to the native memory charge is a missing map, shown by a
A winding that allowed repairs cannot erase

opposite winding does not identify an antiparticle

guarded repair rule preserves both shell degrees, retaining rejected moves as holds. These two winding signs are not identified

svg.text: Choose a question the detector can ask
A position detector reads where the field couples locally. A momentum detector compares translation phases. Each setting has its
own outcome probabilities and back-action. Narrow position support generally broadens momentum; the momentum distribution remains

svg.text: One result becomes a shared record
BORN WEIGHTS AND CONDITIONAL STATE UPDATE
A detector interaction correlates the field with an outcome record. Conditioning on that record gives the state used for later
questions; forgetting the result sums every branch. Comparing records fixes a shared description of the event. It does not let
consensus choose an outcome or fix incompatible observables together.

a.text: Unique Born representation of complete record laws ↗

svg.text: THE EXPERIMENT: WHAT AN OBSERVER ACTUALLY DOES

A preparation makes a reproducible state. An apparatus couples a chosen observable to a pointer. A detector leaves a record. Comparing records makes a shared observation. These are physical processes; neither an observer’s wish nor agreement chooses the outcome.
Supplied four-bin projective instruments. Coherent amplitudes occupy two bins. The two
apparatus settings describe alternative experiments on the same preparation.
A place-sensitive pointer records one position bin.
A Fourier analyzer routes coherent spatial phases to different pointer bins.
The state assigned after a click is conditional on that recorded outcome. Keeping every branch preserves the full probability law. Consensus checks
compatible records and their history; it does not select a preferred click.
p(r) = Tr(ρ Eᵣ), Σ Eᵣ = I
ρᵣ = Kᵣ ρ Kᵣ† / p(r), p(r) > 0

Finite Born uniqueness uses effect-dependent weights and compatible refinements. Native closed histories supply a positive functional; access to arbitrary complex detector effects is an additional bridge.

A sharply localized state has a spread of momentum outcomes. “Undefined” here means no single sharp value, not absence of a momentum distribution. The continuum bound ΔX ΔP ≥ ħ/2 requires the same canonical X and P and their domain; a finite four-bin illustration does not prove that physical identification.
A state carries amplitudes and relative phases. Alternatives add before detection. Constructive and destructive interference change the probability of a click.
Rest mass sets the zero-momentum energy mc² in a justified relativistic sector and common clock. A repair bill or trapped mode frequency needs an energy dictionary before it determines that mass.
Each theorem is a bridge with an entry condition. Read across: what the construction supplies → what follows → what must connect to the same physical state and clock.
A faithful complete reversible twelve-port response closes under commutators in u(H). Proper carrier rotations act by inner automorphisms on that same
response. The compact-Lie classification and fixed-space hypotheses apply.

The transitive A5 action has one fixed line. The centre has dimension one; the centreless su(2)^4 alternative is excluded. The remaining compact semisimple part is su(2)⊕su(3). Hence g≅u(1)⊕su(2)⊕su(3).

Twelve ports alone do not imply this algebra. Lean proves finite dimension/fixed-space arithmetic under explicit centre/classification adapters; the paper supplies the Lie argument. Executable current selection and physical gauge-field attachment are separate.
Finite quantum links + Higgs: [G_a, H] = 0; full fermion currents preserved.

a.text: Exact Gauss interaction and its chiral-field boundary ↗
Gauge paper Theorem3.1: fixed-space Lie-type proof ↗

svg.text: brackets + inner symmetry, not counts alone
The twelve-port icosahedral carrier, uniform native seam repair and the record-recovered slow-band Gram.

The smallest nonzero Laplacian band has rank3. The signed record/control Gram quotient completes to three-dimensional Euclidean coordinates. A separate ordered-spin field construction supplies X and its translation P.
rank 3 carrier → frame; same-field [X, P] = iħ
This local load coordinate is not automatically a particle detector or an inter-carrier 3+1-dimensional spacetime. In the protected one-per-site spin sector, total-load coordinates are scalar.
The binary total-two source with uniform seam/coin law, complete-attempt transfer P, all no-movement attempts, and supplied closed-history length L.
Native counts reconstruct H=-log P and rho_L=P^L/Tr(P^L). Their modular flows share H, with an exact reference-dependent parameter conversion.

Native stochastic P is not its unitary analytic continuation. Modular parameter, repair count, weak-pulse time Nh, host runtime and physical duration are not interchangeable. A tracial state has trivial modular flow.
The clock and ordered-spin field here are different declared sources.

a.text: A native readout separating two clock identifications ↗

svg.text: EVERY FAMILY: SOURCE → FIELD → DYNAMICS → OBSERVATION

These are full dependency chains, including their missing links. The right-hand masses and spins belong to the supplied Standard Model benchmark. No row is a proved identification of an individual OPH defect with a measured species.
The same charge, three configured family slots
The internal lepton doublet and conjugate singlet carry the right charge weights. Their currents act on complete fermionic occupation states. Three family copies are
supplied; they are not three defect types.

svg.text: Mass fields mix into flavor amplitudes
Diagonalization gives ν1, ν2 and ν3. Their mass values are not individually assigned to the νe, νμ and ντ labels. Propagation phases depend on the mass eigenvalues and travel time.
e flavor: not a mass eigenstate
μ flavor: not a mass eigenstate
tau flavor: not a mass eigenstate
Production and detection tag flavor through charged-current partners. Oscillations constrain mass-squared differences and mixing. Absolute masses and Dirac/Majorana character remain undetermined

svg.text: The benchmark supplies a local gauge action and its quantization. The vector A combines W3 and B along the neutral null direction. Gauge constraints leave two physical
No rest-energy term in the unbroken phase
The neutral gauge Hessian has an exact zero eigenvalue under its stated Higgs and gauge assumptions. A wavepacket nevertheless carries energy and momentum. The massless field is not an energy-free
γ: 0 in the SM; bound < 10⁻²⁷ GeV
Localized absorption records implement a detector measurement. Polarization, arrival position and energy distributions require a specified state and detector. A universal sharp particle-position
Gluons: eight directions of an interacting color field
Anti: Real adjoint multiplet; eight color directions
The admitted current algebra supplies non-Abelian color brackets and their action on matter. Counting eight directions alone would not identify a Lie algebra; the
commutators are part of the finite result.
Supply a dynamical color gauge connection
A Yang–Mills connection transports color and interacts with colored matter. The finite quantum-link construction preserves Gauss identities, while its continuum gauge dynamics
and physical state require an additional construction.

Unbroken gauge coefficients, interacting infrared physics
The supplied color-preserving phase gives zero gluon mass parameters. Confinement and color-singlet mass scales concern interacting spectra; a zero gauge coefficient does not imply eight observable
8 gluons: zero gauge mass; no free pole
Scattering and hadronization produce color-singlet records. A gluon contribution is reconstructed through these observables; no free isolated gluon rest-mass measurement is assigned.
Charged weak bosons: W+ and W−
The weak-current algebra contains T+ and T− with opposite electric charges. These operator weights are exact; a propagating vector field is an additional attachment.

With supplied canonical gauge kinetics and Higgs phase, the Z direction is orthogonal to the photon in the vector mass matrix. One Goldstone direction supplies its
Both weak and hypercharge couplings contribute
The nonzero neutral Hessian eigenvalue fixes the quadratic Z mass once g, g′ and v are supplied. This is an exact conditional formula, not a source selection of those parameters.
The displayed Z reference uses a Breit–Wigner convention. A pole definition is a different matched quantity. Its branching fractions and width require the interacting detector response.
Higgs: the radial fluctuation of the selected scalar phase
Anti: Self-conjugate radial scalar in the conditional field theory
The matter grammar admits a weak doublet with hypercharge +1/2. A finite quantum-scalar vertex preserves the same Gauss law. Its three-state carrier is not a selected
Supply a scalar field and a broken phase
The effective action has a positive quartic and a chosen broken-phase vacuum. A gauge-fixed neutral direction describes this phase; it is not a gauge-invariant expectation of
Curvature sets the radial oscillation frequency
Three angular directions join the massive gauge fields. One radial mode is left, with spin zero. Its quadratic rest-energy scale is set by the curvature of the normalized scalar potential.
The Higgs mass is a resonance observable. Decay channels, production rates and widths depend on its interacting couplings and matching; the finite scalar carrier alone supplies none of these

From an action coefficient to a measured mass
Physical kinetic matrices, self-energy, infrared dressing and resonance conventions require additional matching.

svg.text: READ THE MAP WITHOUT LOSING THE SCIENCE
A wave is a coherent state
Alternative amplitudes can interfere before a record distinguishes them. The detector samples the probabilities of its specified instrument; agreement does not supply a missing amplitude law.
A mass is an energy relation
In a relativistic massive sector, energy remains at zero momentum. Repair effort becomes a mass only after deriving its Hamiltonian, common clock, normalization and measured observable.
Finite internal symmetry, a protected memory bit, a winding background and a continuum particle are different objects. The bridges are named so they can be proved or rejected on the same source.
Authenticated v1 scientific inputs: 1402 • No source mass or species claim is promoted by this visual format.
